fixes.explanation: Ezekiel says it plainly: he saw a great many bones on the valley floor, "…and indeed, they were very dry." (Ezekiel 37:2) The LORD led him all around among them, so he got a close look. Hold onto that picture, because it matters for what comes next.

Warm isn't the word the text uses. Ezekiel sees bones on the valley floor, and the text says they were "very dry." (Ezekiel 37:2) Dry is the word, and it sets the stage for what the LORD is about to do.
Stacked isn't what the text pictures, friend. Ezekiel is led all around among the bones on the floor of the valley. What the text tells us about them is that they were "very dry." (Ezekiel 37:2)
Right. Ezekiel sees tendons, flesh and skin, "but there was no breath in them." (Ezekiel 37:8) So they have the look of bodies, but no breathing yet. That missing breath is the detail to hold onto.
Deep sea, that's a bold guess! But no sea in this verse. God tells Ezekiel to say, "Come from the four winds, O breath…" (Ezekiel 37:9) The four winds are where He calls the breath from.
A vast army. Ezekiel says they came to life and stood on their feet, "…a vast army." (Ezekiel 37:10) The valley had been full of bones. Now it's a whole army standing up.

Their graves. God says, "O My people, I will open your graves and bring you up from them…" (Ezekiel 37:12) He says "My people," so these are His own. Opening graves is a big promise, and He says it again in verse 13.
Strength sounds right for a vast army that just stood on its feet. But the verse says, "I will put My Spirit in you and you will live…" (Ezekiel 37:14) God names His Spirit, not strength.
